| [THEORY-553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md) | In the Döring–Isham topos representation of quantum theory a bounded physical quantity cannot take values in the topos's real-number object; it is represented faithfully by an arrow from the spectral presheaf to a presheaf of monotone real functions over subcontexts, so its value at a context is a spread that widens as the context shrinks, and these values form only a commutative monoid, under which sums of daseinised quantities are not daseinisations of sums | Döring & Isham, paper III (2007/8), [LIT-299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md) ([NOTE-290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md)), restated with additions in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The Gel'fand transforms of daseinised operators grow as contexts shrink, so arrows into the constant presheaf ℝ are impossible (3.3–3.4). Each Â gives a natural transformation δ̆^o(A) : Σ → ℝ^⪰ (Thm 3.1), and Â ↦ δ̆^o(A) is injective, by de Groote's results. ℝ^⪰ is a monoid, not a group; differences need a group completion, whose global elements are the functions of bounded variation on the context poset. No choice among the candidate value objects is made, and the state-dependent reading of the spread is cited, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md) | In Kolmogorovian probability, joint distributedness is transitive, so representing a measurement by one random variable in every context it occurs in already puts all measurements of a connected system on one probability space; within that representation a Kochen–Specker or Bell contradiction refutes the context-independent identification of measurements, not the existence of a joint distribution | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md), read in full in [NOTE-623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-623.md). The transitivity step is an elementary proof; the reading of the reductio is an argument that rests on it. It binds the random-variable representation only: the sheaf account keeps one variable per measurement and asks whether marginals glue, and a reader who holds that view is not bound by it. The paper also proves that a coupling of a binary connection is multimaximal iff adjacent pairs, ordered by their means, are maximally coupled (Theorem II.3). | Active |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v2 | From a symmetric, positivity-preserving, positive semi-definite affinity, the normalized Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, so its leading eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data with Euclidean distance equal to diffusion distance, and a density-corrected normalization recovers the Laplace–Beltrami operator independently of how the data were sampled | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) from extracted text whose displayed equations were not visible. The construction and the embedding are standard. The convergence theorem and the α-family are stated without proof, which is deferred to a companion paper. [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) filed no THEORY for those reasons. It is filed Proposed on the owner's ruling that a well-established result may rest on a skim when it is not wrong as stated. Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and the paper's "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v2 | In Ganea et al.'s hyperbolic neural networks, linear maps and nonlinearities are Euclidean ones read through the chart at the origin, so a stack of them without biases is a Euclidean network conjugated by that chart, and the curvature acts only through the bias translations and the distance-based output layer | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md) | Whatever redundancy measure a partial information decomposition uses, provided its atoms satisfy the consistency equation, the average number of single sources an atom can be read from is Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) and the average number of sources it cannot do without is Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y); so the redundancy–synergy index equals (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y), and for three or more sources it counts a k-way redundancy k − 1 times but synergy once | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md), read in full in [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md), with the combinatorial proofs of Props. 1–4 and 6 checked by hand. The averages need only the consistency equation and I(X;Y) > 0; reading them as average degrees, and the bounds of Appendix B, need non-negative atoms. Corollary 5 overstates Prop. 6 (⇔ for ⇐). The network results are on tiny quantised models evaluated on their own training sets, and are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | The structural width of Xin Li's learning programme is a covering number of the margin-safe region by local pieces: its lower bounds come from metric confinement through a wedge point, not from topology, labels enter only through the margin, and the error floor below width binds only learners assembled from local experts, so it does not entail routing, nor training routing apart from the task loss | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-576](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-576.md) | In a bundled network, one fiber graph attached at a single node to every node of a base graph, the low Laplacian spectrum is the base spectrum divided by the fiber size to first order, so the gap exponent (Fiedler dimension) is set by the base while the density-of-states exponent (spectral dimension) is the fiber's; the two come apart generically and coincide only in special cases, and relaxation then decays with the spectral dimension at intermediate times but equilibrates on a time set by the Fiedler dimension | Grimaldi, Villegas, Vezzani, Burioni, Cassi & Gabrielli (2025; PRE Letter 2026), [LIT-028](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-028.md), read in full with its SM in [NOTE-005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-005.md), which re-derived the key steps and checked them numerically on the comb. λ_{n1} = ℓ^b_{n1}/N_f gives d_g = 2(d_f,f + d_f,b)/(d_f,f + 2d_f,b/d_g,b) in the base-controlled regime; d_s = d_s,f is earlier work by the same group. The comb has d_s = 1 and d_g = 4/3. Proved for one graph class only; the paper's composite finite-size scaling prefactors (SM Eqs. 25, 29) are wrong, and its "generic property of composite architectures" outruns the proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v2 | In the Döring–Isham scheme for realising collections of systems in topoi, disjoint sums of quantum systems compose exactly; along a tensor product of finite-dimensional systems, the pull-back of a constituent's quantity agrees with the composite's own quantity at a context exactly when every projection in it with proper support on the first factor has the form P⊗1, so it fails for every non-scalar quantity and no operator on the composite realises the pull-back | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). Classical physics satisfies the translation condition (3.18) exactly. For quantum disjoint sums the pull-back of δ̆(A₁⊕A₂) is δ̆(A₁) (Lemma 4.2, 4.24; checked). For H₁⊗H₂ the pull-back gives δ(Â₁)_{V_W}⊗1̂ at each context W, which equals δ(Â₁⊗1̂)_W on contexts V₁⊗ℂ1̂. That it differs elsewhere, and that no operator realises it, are asserted. The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md) | Every unital Banach *-algebra satisfying Gelfand and Naimark's norm conditions is isometrically *-isomorphic to a norm-closed algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, built from positive functionals by what is now the GNS construction, and a commutative one is the algebra of all continuous functions on its compact maximal-ideal space | Gelfand & Naimark (1943), [LIT-313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md), read in full in [NOTE-303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-303.md). Theorem 1 embeds every normed *-ring in B(H) for a Hilbert space not assumed separable; Lemma 1 is the commutative case, resting on Gelfand's 1941 paper and Šilov's boundary. The paper never says "C*-algebra" or "GNS". It assumes two axioms it suspected redundant, and notes that a single norm identity may replace two others. It gives the object-level isomorphism R ≅ C(𝔐), not a categorical duality, and nothing on uniqueness or irreducibility of the representation. | Active |
| [THEORY-595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-595.md) | A filter over a set of worlds is a finitely consistent propositional theory and an ultrafilter a negation-complete one; read so, the ultrafilter extension theorem is Lindenbaum's lemma for propositions, and Łoś's theorem builds a model that makes true exactly what an ultrafilter says, which proves first-order compactness without proof theory, given the axiom of choice | Turner (preprint 2021, published 2025), [LIT-145](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-145.md), read in [NOTE-177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md). An expository paper: "None of the results are novel" (p. 2). Maximal, prime and ultra filters coincide (Thm 2); every filter extends to an ultrafilter (Thm 3); Łoś's theorem (Thm 9); compactness (Thm 12). The results are standard and correct, though the write-up has slips. A filter is only finitely consistent, and that is the point. The pairings with Lindenbaum and Henkin are analogies, not reductions. | Active |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most mathematical dualities are adjunctions between one category and the opposite of another, which become dual equivalences on their fixed points; what makes them dualities rather than equivalences is the reversal of arrows, so many of the 'dualities' physicists name are, in the mathematician's sense, equivalences or symmetries | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) | Neural circuits that must represent hierarchically organised states in few dimensions use a hyperbolic geometry, three-dimensional where it has been measured, because hyperbolic space holds exponentially many well-separated states within a small radius; the argument from Zipf's law to this geometry does not hold, and the evidence is two Betti-curve studies tested only against uniform Euclidean nulls | Sharpee (2019), [LIT-875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), read in [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md): a four-page programmatic review with no new result, whose reading filed no THEORY because its claims are conjectures. Filed here as Proposed because the record holds two tests of the conjecture, odour statistics ([LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md)) and CA1 place-cell correlations ([LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md), [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)), and no general statement. The Zipf step shows a shared exponential count of states, which any system with extensive entropy has, not a shared metric, and the rigidity argument for three dimensions cites Mostow's theorem, which concerns finite-volume manifolds and says nothing about noisy point clouds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Over the poset of commutative von Neumann subalgebras, coarse-graining a projector to a smaller subalgebra is exactly the direct image of its clopen region of the Gelfand spectrum under restriction, so the coarse-graining presheaf is the presheaf of clopen spectral regions; and a quantum state's sieve-valued truth values are fixed by one coherent family of regions, its supports: a proposition is true at a subcontext exactly when the support there lies under the coarse-grained proposition | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. Theorem 3.1 shows that any assignment defined by "support ≤ coarse-grained proposition", with supports forming a global element of G, is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC; a state's supports qualify. Both theorems are close to definitional. Nothing here builds Heyting operations on clopen sub-objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-620](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-620.md) | Walsh's 1923 functions are a closed orthonormal set on (0, 1) of ±1-valued step functions, each a parity of finitely many binary digits, whose expansions behave like Fourier series: grouped uniform convergence for continuous functions, convergence under bounded variation, localisation, Cesàro summability, and divergence at any chosen point for some continuous function | Walsh (1923), [LIT-300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-300.md), read in full in [NOTE-281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-281.md), with the explicit formula and the Lebesgue-constant recurrence checked for small n. Closure is inherited from Haar's system, to which Walsh's is related by an orthogonal change of basis within each dyadic level. Theorems II–X give the Fourier-like convergence theory. The paper never mentions groups or characters: that these functions are the characters of the Cantor group, and of the Boolean cube on n digits, is a later identification. | Active |
| [THEORY-629](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md) | Every continuous linear functional on a Hilbert space is the inner product with a unique vector of the same norm, given in any orthonormal basis by the conjugated values of the functional on the basis; completeness is what makes it so, and Riesz's 1907 statement on L² asserted only that a representing function exists | Adler (2021), [LIT-243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md), read in full in [NOTE-854](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-854.md): two complete proofs, by projection (Thm 3.5) and by an orthonormal basis (Thm 4.9), with completeness used once, in the projection theorem. Riesz (1907), [LIT-326](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-326.md), read in [NOTE-289](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-289.md), is the priority note: existence of k with U(f) = ∫ f k for continuous linear U on square-summable functions, stated without proof, uniqueness or norm. The theorem says nothing about kernels, factorisation or uniqueness of representations. Both readings advise citing a textbook for anything leaned on. | Active |
| [THEORY-642](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md) | Basic two-level type theory, an inner homotopy type theory with an outer level of strict equality, is conservative over homotopy type theory, so an inner type it proves inhabited is already inhabited in HoTT, but a fibrant-replacement type former would force uniqueness of identity proofs on the inner level | Annenkov, Capriotti, Kraus & Sattler (2017; MSCS 2023), [LIT-095](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md), whose §§1–3 were read in full in [NOTE-047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-047.md), the reading of the nLab page it supersedes ([LIT-040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md)). Props 2.18–2.19 prove that inhabitation of inner types is reflected, through a presheaf model over any model of HoTT. Thm 2.20 proves that a fibrant-replacement former implies UIP for inner types. The conservativity is the weak, inhabitation-reflecting kind. Results that use the axioms relating the two levels' natural numbers, which untruncated semisimplicial types need, are not known to transfer. | Active |
| [THEORY-645](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-645.md) | A countable discrete abelian group and a compact second-countable abelian group can each be recovered as the character group of the other, and a locally compact, connected, second-countable abelian group is a compact group plus ℝʳ; Pontryagin's 1934 paper does not prove duality for general locally compact abelian groups | Pontryagin (1934), [LIT-333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-333.md), read in full in [NOTE-284](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-284.md). Theorem 5 and the First Fundamental Theorem give the duality between countable discrete and compact second-countable abelian groups, with characters valued in ℝ/ℤ. The compact half rests on Peter–Weyl with Haar measure, used to extract one-dimensional characters. The Second and Third Fundamental Theorems are structure theorems, not duality. Commutative only; for non-abelian groups the relevant object is Peter–Weyl, and characters are traces, not homomorphisms. General locally compact duality is van Kampen's (1935). | Active |
| [THEORY-652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-652.md) | Over any field, a finite-dimensional associative algebra with no nilpotent two-sided ideal is uniquely a direct sum of simple algebras, and each simple algebra is a full matrix algebra over a division algebra, which over the reals can be the complex numbers or the quaternions | Wedderburn (1908), [LIT-309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-309.md), read in full in [NOTE-280](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-280.md). Thm 17 with Thm 10 gives the unique decomposition into simple algebras; Thms 20–22 build n² matrix units from primitive idempotents and give simple = primitive × full matrix algebra. Primitive here means one idempotent, which makes the factor a division algebra once semisimple (Thm 15). The field is arbitrary, which was the paper's novelty. That the centre is spanned by the block identities follows from Thm 23's corollary; the paper never says "centre". The general splitting of an algebra into nilpotent plus semisimple parts is claimed in the summary but proved only in special cases. | Active |
| [THEORY-654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-654.md) | For full-state linear-quadratic regulation of a single-input plant, the return-difference identity keeps the sensitivity at or below 1 at every frequency, so the loop tolerates any gain increase, a gain cut to one half and at least 60° of phase error for any Q ≥ 0 and r > 0; the guarantee does not carry over when the state is replaced by an observer's estimate | Başar, Meyn & Perkins (2020), [LIT-051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-051.md), graduate course notes read in full in [NOTE-062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-062.md), with every worked example recomputed. §10.6 derives \|1 + L(jω)\|² = 1 + \|P(jω)\|²/r ≥ 1 for the full-state loop, hence \|S\| ≤ 1 and the classical margins. The derivation is for one input; the multi-input version needs more, which the notes do not discuss. The Pendubot thread shows a controllable, observable plant whose one-sensor observer-based design has gain margin below 10⁻². The result is Kalman's and standard; the notes are an adequate free citation for it. | Active |
| [THEORY-664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md) | In a finite-dimensional probabilistic theory with unrestricted effects and local tomography, if every system can steer each of its own states from a composite with a copy of itself, every irreducible state space is homogeneous and weakly self-dual; steering does not yet give strong self-duality, so it stops short of the Jordan-algebraic and quantum state spaces | Barnum, Gaebler & Wilce (2009), [LIT-081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), read in full in [NOTE-082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-082.md). A bipartite state steers its marginal iff its map on effects is a strong quotient of order intervals (Thm 5.4). With matching dimensions a steering state is an order-isomorphism, and a cone is homogeneous iff every interior state purifies to an isomorphism state (Thm 4.1). Hence universal self-steering gives homogeneity and weak self-duality (Prop. 5.8). The weaker Prop. 5.7 is thinly argued. The C*-algebraic conclusion of §6 needs strong self-duality, which the paper assumes rather than derives. | Active |
| [THEORY-685](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-685.md) | The Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture fails for every compact C² hypersurface with a point of non-zero curvature: for each large R a function and a weight violate it by a factor of order log R, which refutes Stein's conjecture as stated and closes the Mizohata–Takeuchi route to loss-free endpoint multilinear restriction | Cairo (2025), [LIT-030](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-030.md), read in full in [NOTE-051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-051.md), which checked the counting and exponent bookkeeping. The paper states the theorem for any C² hypersurface not lying in a hyperplane; the proof needs a curved point, which a connected such surface has. The incidence lemma (§4) is the step a non-specialist could not verify. The loss is log R, not a power, and the counterexample is a family indexed by R. It does not refute endpoint multilinear restriction itself. Its proposed local replacement has since been refuted with power loss on a dense family of surfaces, per the abstract of a later paper. | Active |
| [THEORY-686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md) v2 | An observation modelled as a monotone map between preorders can show of a joined system more than the join of its observations of the parts, and out of a preorder with all joins the observations that preserve all joins, the empty join and infinite joins included, are exactly the left adjoints | Fong & Spivak (2018), [LIT-803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), Chapter 1, read closely in a Skimmed NOTE ([NOTE-601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-601.md)) whose other chapters were seen only at their openings. Def. 1.93, after Adam, defines a generative effect as Φ(a) ∨ Φ(b) < Φ(a ∨ b). Prop. 1.111 and Thm 1.115 give that left adjoints preserve all joins and, from a source with all joins, only they do. The results are standard order theory, re-derived by the record because NOTE-601 is a skim. The absence of generative effects is weaker than preserving all joins, and does not characterise the left adjoints. | Active |
| [THEORY-697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) | Sparse distributed memory's read weights each stored pattern by the number of hard locations within the read radius of both query and pattern, a ball-intersection count that falls roughly exponentially in Hamming distance over a local window, so softmax attention over cosine similarity of unit-norm queries and keys, with a fitted inverse temperature, approximates the SDM read there; the approximation cannot hold globally, since the binary count vanishes beyond twice the radius, and its inverse temperature comes from a regression, not from the paper's analytic bound | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), read in full in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), which re-evaluated the intersection formula and the fit. The exact intersection (Eq. 2) is checked against Kanerva's lune formula and simulation; eight SDM and fitted-softmax variants retrieve almost identically on random patterns, MNIST and CIFAR-10, with three named exceptions. The intersection is a staircase in distance, the fit holds to about dv = 20 for d = 15, the analytic β of App. B.2 is about 2–2.5 times too small, and every optimal radius assumes random patterns and addresses. The GPT-2 "confirmation" and the cerebellar implementation of attention are argument, not demonstration. | Active |
| [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) | Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). Theorem 1 is the basic theorem of formal concept analysis applied to the crisp relation got by thresholding Fisher-LDA probes, and it holds for every binary relation; the paper's own proof plan says so. The empirical content is that the thresholded probes on three 7–8B models agree with a GPT-4o-annotated incidence at macro F1 69.7–83.2 and predict WordNet subsumption at F1 57.1–77.1. No closure, absorption or recovered-lattice comparison is tested, and the paper's join is not a lattice join as written. It is not evidence that language models encode a lattice beyond the incidence. | Active |
| [THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md) | No redundancy measure on the Williams–Beer partial-information lattice can satisfy symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, the identity axiom and non-negative atoms once there are three sources: for two independent bits, their XOR and a target that copies all three, identity forces three one-bit atoms under a two-bit total, so one atom is at most −1 bit, and a multivariate decomposition that keeps identity must give up non-negativity or the lattice | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich & Jost (2014), [LIT-1202](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), read in full in [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md). A proved impossibility, checked by hand and by script. It also uses invariance of redundancy under relabelling the target, which is not stated as an axiom. I_min escapes it by failing identity, Ince's I_ccs by accepting the −1-bit atom. | Active |
| [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof. With n states and finite outcome sets, write experiments as n × N Markov matrices P and Q. Every risk vector Q attains in every decision problem is attainable with P exactly when Q = PM for some Markov matrix M. The arbitrary-outcome extension is [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), still Proposed. A qualitative order: most pairs are incomparable, and it says nothing about how far apart they are. | Active |
| [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | In a linear-in-parameters model with Gaussian noise and a Gaussian prior, the evidence is exactly the best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor set by the posterior curvature, and when the design grows linearly with n that factor costs (k/2) log n | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md) | On a complex Hilbert space no orthonormal basis or tensor factorisation of given dimensions is distinguished by the space alone, and orthonormal bases correspond exactly to commutative special †-Frobenius algebras; over the reals that correspondence fails | Three results [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) rested on, held apart from its synthesis. (a) The unitary group acts transitively on the orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and on its tensor factorisations of given dimensions, so neither is fixed by the space; a non-degenerate self-adjoint operator fixes a basis up to phases, and its invariant content is its spectrum. (b) Over ℂ, commutative special †-Frobenius algebras correspond exactly to orthonormal bases: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, [LIT-274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), Thm 5.1 and §6, in finite dimension; Abramsky & Heunen, [LIT-275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), Thm 22, for the non-unital ones satisfying the H*-axiom, in any dimension. (c) Over ℝ it fails: ℂ as a real algebra, with multiplication scaled by 1/√2, is a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero copyable vector. | Active |
| [THEORY-722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md) | In Contextuality-by-Default 2.0, whether a system of non-binary variables is contextual depends on which variables represent the measurements: coarse-graining can turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one, while for connections of two variables, and for consistently connected systems, CbD 1.0 and 2.0 agree | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md), Examples 1–3 and Section 4, read in [NOTE-643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-643.md) (claims C4 and C6). Under multimaximal couplings, lumping values of non-binary variables can destroy every multimaximal coupling, so a noncontextual system becomes contextual. The verdict on a fixed set of measurements therefore depends on which variables represent them. For connections of two variables, hence cyclic systems, and for consistently connected systems, the 1.0 and 2.0 definitions agree. It does not say the coupling choice changes verdicts in larger connections, which is [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md)'s asserted part. | Active |
| [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. What is observed fixes a representation only up to that observation's symmetry group: a centred linear kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal map ([THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)), and a softmax output distribution up to an invertible linear map of the embedding with the inverse transpose on the unembedding (Thm 2.2). KL can go to zero while the embeddings stay non-linearly related (Thm 3.1, Cor. 3.2), but d_LLV ≤ ε gives d_f,g ≤ 2Mε (Thm 4.7). Final layer only. It does not say what the Platonic hypothesis means; that is [THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md) | For a linear system du/dt = A(t)u, non-normality is necessary for time dependence to destabilize an operator that is uniformly stable at every instant, and a non-normal operator neutral at every instant can be asymptotically unstable under switching | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), eq. 12 and §4, read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Because d‖u‖²/dt = u†(A + A†)u, the first Lyapunov exponent lies between the long-run averages of the extreme eigenvalues of the Hermitian part. For a normal operator the largest is the spectral abscissa, so an operator that is normal and uniformly stable at every instant has a negative exponent. A switched undamped oscillator, neutral at every instant, has a positive exponent. The stochastic genericity results are [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is a nuclear-norm penalty on their product: with tied weights λ‖W‖²_F = λ‖WWᵀ‖_*, and for untied factors the least (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over UVᵀ = M is ‖M‖_*, so for any loss that sees the weights only through the product, square-penalized training is nuclear-norm-penalized training of a product of bounded rank | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-727](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-727.md) | For a fixed linear operator in an inner-product norm, growth over time t is the top singular value of the propagator, which the eigenvalues bound only from below; it starts at the numerical abscissa, which can be positive when every mode decays; and the forced response is bounded by the condition number of the eigenvectors over the distance to the spectrum | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). For du/dt = Au with A fixed: a normal A grows as its spectral abscissa; in general the growth over t is σ_max(e^(At)), with the eigenvalues as a floor; the initial growth rate is the top eigenvalue of (A + A†)/2; and harmonic forcing is bounded by κ(E)/dist(iω, Λ(A)), with the ε-pseudospectrum marking where eigenvalues of A + Δ, ‖Δ‖ < ε, can go. All in a chosen norm. The white-noise variance result is [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) | On a finite data set, a symmetric positive affinity normalized to a Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, and its eigenvectors scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals the diffusion distance weighted by the inverse stationary law | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), skimmed in [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md), with the derivation written out here because the paper's equations were not seen. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-729](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md) | An adjunction between a category and the opposite of another restricts to a dual equivalence between the full subcategories on which its unit and counit are isomorphisms | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), §3, read in full in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md), with the proof the paper omits written out here. For F : C → D^op left adjoint to G : D^op → C, let C′ and D′ be the full subcategories on which the unit and the counit are isomorphisms. Then F and G restrict to inverse equivalences C′ ≃ D′, and D′ is a full subcategory of D^op, so C′ is dually equivalent to a full subcategory of D. Pontrjagin duality is the example. That most dualities are of this form is [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md)'s thesis, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) | For an embedding whose Gram matrix is the absolute co-occurrence deviation matrix at full rank, words on a periodic lattice whose positive and negative co-occurrence parts each depend only on separation have Fourier modes of the lattice as principal components, in degenerate cos/sin pairs with amplitude the square root of the kernel's Fourier transform, and the exponential kernel gives a closed loop with integer frequencies on a periodic lattice and an open curve with non-integer frequencies on an interval | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-731](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-731.md) | For softmax cross-entropy with balanced classes, the Gauss–Newton matrix splits exactly into four positive semidefinite second-moment terms, the class-centre term has rank at most C with eigenvectors in the span of the class centres and the spectrum of a C × C Gram matrix, and so the k-th eigenvalue of the whole is never below the k-th eigenvalue of the class-centre term | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md), read in [NOTE-479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-479.md). Exact algebra, re-derived here. For softmax cross-entropy, the Gauss–Newton matrix is G = (1/n)ΔΔᵀ, an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. Grouping them gives G = G₀ + G₁ + G₂ + G₃, with every term positive semidefinite. G₁, the class-centre term, has rank at most C, and its spectrum is read from a C × C Gram matrix. So λ_k(G) ≥ λ_k(G₁ + G₂) ≥ λ_k(G₁) for every k, in any network, trained or not. That G₁ carries the outliers of trained networks is measured, not derived, and stays Proposed in [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md) | For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): the VAR form (3.26) of exact dynamical independence, with the genericity count of §3.3 made a proof for VAR order p ≥ 2 and corrected for p = 1. Linear coarse-grainings Y = LX of a stable VAR with non-degenerate Gaussian innovations only. It says nothing about near-independence, about the multimodality of the dynamical-dependence cost, or about nonlinear maps. | Active |
| [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) | In the hyperbolic plane, a root carrying deg_max ≥ 15 chains of length m, embedded with worst-case distortion 1 + ε for ε ≤ 1, forces some node to hyperbolic distance at least (ℓ/(4ε))·ln(deg_max/(π√2)) from the origin, so fixed-point Poincaré coordinates need Ω((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. Only the root's children are used to fix the embedding's scale c, and then the chains turn the scale into depth. Plane only, one family of trees, fixed-point coordinates in the Poincaré disk, deg_max ≥ 15 and ε ≤ 1. It says nothing about H^r for r > 2, or about whether any tree needs fewer bits under another number system. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Under a local quadratic model of the loss with the greedy optimal step, per-step progress at batch size B is ΔL_max/(1 + B_noise/B), and at fixed B the steps and examples needed satisfy (S/S_min − 1)(E/E_min − 1) = 1, with E_min/S_min the progress-weighted mean of B_noise | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) | Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) | A two-layer ReLU student of width at least kM, fitting an orthonormal teacher of M neurons on the sphere, has for any k global minima a global minimum joined to each by a two-piece linear path of minima; and in a deep linear network of depth L and width above 1 + r(L − 1), any r global minima in general position share a global minimum linearly connected to each | Lin, Li and Wu (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), Theorems 6, 11 and 18 with Lemmas 7 and 25, read in [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) and re-derived by the promotion audit. Two toy models whose minima can be written down: a two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal teacher on the sphere at population loss, and a deep linear network fitting y = Qx. Spare width lets every minimum be moved, along segments of minima, to one a common centre can reach. No permutation symmetry is used, and nothing is claimed about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md) v2 | As the kernel width ε goes to 0, Coifman and Lafon's α-normalized diffusion operator (I − P_{ε,α})/ε, for data sampled with density q = e^{−U} from a compact manifold without boundary, converges uniformly on smooth functions, at rate O(ε), to Δf + 2(1 − α)⟨∇U, ∇f⟩ with Δ the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator, which is minus the generator of a reversible diffusion with drift −2(1 − α)∇U and invariant density proportional to q^{2(1−α)}; α = 0 gives potential 2U and invariant density q², α = 1/2 gives the Langevin dynamics whose invariant density is the sampling density itself, and α = 1 gives Brownian motion on the manifold, with no trace of the density | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md), with the PNAS announcement [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md). The paper states the limit as a Schrödinger operator. Written as a drift, it shows what each α keeps of the density: the walk's stationary density is q^{2(1−α)}. On a manifold without boundary the limit is derived in full, the kernel expansion included (re-derived on promotion, 2026-10-20). The paper's own α = 1/2 display has a sign error. Its boundary rate and heat-kernel proof are incomplete and are left to [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-745](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md) | For the reversible walk p = k/d built from a symmetric non-negative kernel on a finite connected set, the t-step diffusion distance is exactly the Euclidean distance between the coordinates λ_l^t ψ_l, and keeping only the coordinates with \|λ_l\|^t > δ\|λ₁\|^t errs in D_t² by at most δ²\|λ₁\|^{2t}(1/π(x) + 1/π(y)), an absolute bound and not the relative accuracy δ that Coifman and Lafon state; the truncated maps are nested as t grows, so with δ fixed the steps t order a refinement chain by eigenvalue modulus, while untruncated they are all invertible images of one another | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in full in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md). The identity D_t² = Σ λ_l^{2t}(ψ_l(x) − ψ_l(y))² is exact. The paper's Proposition 1 says the truncated map keeps it "up to relative accuracy δ". The true bound is absolute and can be large relative to D_t for nearby points. In the refinement sense, the diffusion-map family coarsens with t only through the threshold. Finite sets, counting measure and reversible walks only. It says nothing about the manifold limit or about non-reversible chains. | Active |
| [THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md) | Over a fixed finite set of basis functions, slow feature analysis is a generalized eigenproblem: the outputs that minimize ⟨ẏ²⟩ under zero mean, unit variance and decorrelation are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the derivative covariance against the covariance, in order of slowness, and a stack of such stages, each of whose function spaces contains its inputs, can only keep or lower each of its first m slowness values on the training signal, and may keep them | Wiskott and Sejnowski (2002), [LIT-1249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1249.md), read in full in [NOTE-971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-971.md). Within the span of a fixed basis, the slowest decorrelated unit-variance outputs are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the pencil (⟨ż̃ż̃ᵀ⟩, cov z̃), and each output's slowness is its eigenvalue. A consequence the paper does not draw: a stack of such stages whose function spaces contain their inputs is never faster at a higher stage, componentwise, on the training signal, so in this model "higher is slower" is imposed by the objective, weakly, and can stall. It is about the training signal and a fixed function space. It says nothing about test data, about a generative model, about invariance as opposed to slowness, or about learning dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | In Fourier–Galerkin large-eddy simulation, a first-order finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure tracks filtered-DNS energy decay and dissipation on the viscous Burgers equation and on the incompressible Taylor–Green vortex, isotropic turbulence and channel flow about as well as dynamic Smagorinsky where that model is at home and better than Smagorinsky and the t-model on the transitional Taylor–Green vortex; the memory length that fits it is set by the cutoff, not by the flow alone, scaling in Burgers roughly as 0.2 over the spectral radius of the resolved variables' Jacobian | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) v3 | A weak solution of the incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box that lies in L³(0,T; B^α_{3,∞}) ∩ C([0,T]; L²) with α > 1/3 conserves kinetic energy, because the energy flux into scales below a mollification scale ε is bounded by Cε^(3α−1)∫‖u‖³ and so vanishes as ε → 0; this does not show that rougher solutions dissipate | Constantin, E and Titi (1994), [LIT-1248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1248.md), read in [NOTE-982](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-982.md). The positive half of Onsager's conjecture, in the Besov form: if velocity increments obey ‖u(·+y) − u‖_{L³} ≤ C\|y\|^α with α > 1/3, integrated in time, the coarse-grained energy flux across scale ε is O(ε^(3α−1)) and no energy can be lost to vanishing scales. It is a statement about regular fields only. It does not show that a flux survives the limit for rougher ones: that energy can fail to be conserved below 1/3 is Isett's later theorem ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)), that it can strictly decrease is Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol's (THEORY-776), both Proposed, and some rough solutions conserve energy anyway. | Active |
| [THEORY-751](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-751.md) v2 | For a memoryless source with finite alphabets and a per-letter distortion, a description at rate R(D₁) can be refined to distortion D₂ < D₁ at total rate R(D₂) iff some pair of rate–distortion-optimal test channels forms a Markov chain X → X̂₂ → X̂₁; the condition holds for every discrete source under Hamming distortion and fails for some three-letter sources under absolute error | Equitz and Cover (1991), [LIT-1238](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1238.md), read in [NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md), with every step re-derived by 2026-10-20. Lossless two-stage description is possible exactly when the coarse optimum is a stochastic degradation of the fine optimum. That is a Markov chain on test channels, not nesting of partitions, and it is an asymptotic block-coding statement. It does not say that optimal single-shot quantizers or deterministic encoders nest, and the paper's own Gaussian example shows they need not. It says nothing yet about the information bottleneck beyond a formal transfer through the KL distortion. | Active |
| [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md) | In optimal prediction of a Hamiltonian system with separable energy and canonical initial law, projected by conditional expectation, the t-model's leading-order memory term tPLQLx makes the effective Hamiltonian of the resolved variables non-increasing, so the eliminated variables' memory enters as a damping that grows linearly in time | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2002), [LIT-1253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1253.md), read in [NOTE-975](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-975.md): Theorem 8.1. Truncating the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral at its lag-zero value gives dΦ/dt = R̄(Φ) + tS(Φ), and under the stated conditions this dissipates the free energy of the resolved variables. It says nothing about how well the t-model predicts, gives no error bound, and holds only for the conditional-expectation projection; the true conditional mean's effective energy need not decrease. | Active |
| [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) | For finite X and Y, the information bottleneck is successively refinable from budget λ₁ to λ₂ > λ₁ iff some pair of optimal encoders forms a Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, that is, iff the coarse optimal encoder is a garbling of a fine one; when the fine optimum's decoder points q(X\|t₂) are affinely independent, this holds for that pair iff every decoder point q(X\|t₁) of the coarse optimum lies in their convex hull, so a failed hull test on optima that are unique up to merging and relabelling proves that refinement fails | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). It turns [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md)'s Markov formulation into a finite check: nesting between two IB optima is a convex-hull inclusion of their decoder points, which a linear programme decides. The check is on given optima, and refinability asks for some pair. So a failed check settles the question only when the optima are certified globally optimal and unique. This entry adds that the information bottleneck's own convex-envelope dual can supply that certificate. Finite alphabets, two stages. | Active |
| [THEORY-754](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md) v2 | If a velocity field's third-order increments obey ‖δu(r)‖₃ ≤ C u_rms (r/L)^σ at every separation r, with 0 < σ < 1, then for a smooth, rapidly decaying filter the space-averaged energy flux across scale ℓ takes at most a fraction of order (ℓ/Δ)^(1−σ) from strain at scales above Δ and of order (δ/ℓ)^(2σ) from stress at scales below δ, measured against u_rms³/L·(ℓ/L)^(3σ−1); so transfer between scales is local in scale, with a power-law decay and no gap | Eyink and Aluie (2009), [LIT-1239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1239.md), read in [NOTE-969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-969.md), stating bounds proved in Eyink (2005), [LIT-1252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1252.md). A conditional inequality: if velocity increments scale no faster than r^σ in the L³ mean, the contributions of far larger and far smaller scales to the mean flux across ℓ are bounded by powers of the scale ratio. It needs 0 < σ < 1: σ < 1 for the large scales, σ > 0 for the small. That the inertial range satisfies the hypothesis, that the mean flux there is non-zero, and the sharper 4/3 exponent are assumptions or heuristics, not part of it. It is about one field decomposed by scale, and says nothing about units. | Active |
| [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md) v3 | For a linear system x(t+1) = Ax and a partition of its variables, the vector of block sums evolves autonomously from every initial state iff the partition is column-equitable, every column of each block of A summing to the same value; the aggregate operator then keeps a subset of A's eigenvalues, and the blocks may interact as strongly as they like, so exact aggregation is not decomposition | Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Hermisson (2004), [LIT-1242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1242.md), read in [NOTE-979](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-979.md). Exact aggregation of a linear system by the sums over a partition holds for every state iff the partition is column-equitable, a symmetry condition, not a weak-coupling one. Linear dynamics and partition-based aggregation only. It says nothing about approximate aggregation, the Simon–Ando case, or nonlinear systems, where the paper itself shows aggregations with no linear counterpart. | Active |
| [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) | The information bottleneck is successively refinable between every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X, by nested erasures of Y, and when X and Y are both binary, where the optimum at each nonzero budget is unique up to merging and relabelling and its two decoder points are the ends of an interval of the source simplex that only widens as the budget grows | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). These are the two finite cases in which nested information-bottleneck optima are guaranteed at every pair of budgets. Neither reaches the record's four-state source, whose Y is not a function of X and whose X has three effective states. [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md) finds that source not refinable. So binary Y alone does not guarantee nesting. The function case is the degenerate one, where the bottleneck is just a noisy copy of Y. | Active |
| [THEORY-758](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md) | For a self-adjoint diffusion operator T with spectrum in [0, 1], the diffusion-wavelet levels are spectral subspaces spanned by the eigenvectors with λ^s ≥ ε for an increasing sequence of powers s, so they form an exactly nested chain of T-invariant subspaces whose differences are bands of the spectrum, about one octave each, not spatial blocks; Coifman and Maggioni's compressed algorithm, which squares the operator on each orthonormal basis, thresholds T^{2^{j−1}} at level j and not T^{2^j−1} as the paper states; and since each level is T-invariant, each is an exactly closed linear coarse-graining whose localized basis is a choice the level does not fix | Coifman and Maggioni (2006), [LIT-1256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1256.md), read in full in [NOTE-984](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-984.md). The levels of a diffusion multiresolution are spectral bands. Nesting is exact and needs no decay of the spectrum, and decay buys only compression. The compressed algorithm as written keeps ⟨ξ : λ^{2^{j−1}} > ε⟩ at level j, and the paper's own Fig. 9 follows this, not its stated count. Each level closes exactly under T, but a single scaling function does not. It says nothing about non-self-adjoint operators, about error bounds for the compressed scheme with finite precision, or about when a localized basis exists. | Active |
| [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md) | The finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure that Parish and Duraisamy take from Stinis, truncated at order m with one trapezoidal sub-interval and constant memory lengths, is a finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation: m + 1 auxiliary variables per resolved mode, each relaxing at rate 2/τ; at first order it replaces the memory integral by the kernel 2e^{−2s/τ₀} acting on the first-order term, which tends to τ₀ times that term, the t-model with t replaced by τ₀, when τ₀ is short against the resolved dynamics; its kernel is twice the true one at zero lag for every τ₀, so it is not exact even where the true memory is a single exponential, and nothing in the construction bounds its error | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The finite-memory closure turns the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral into auxiliary ordinary differential equations, so the reduced model is the resolved variables plus finitely many memory coordinates: the shape of augmentation [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks about. But the truncation drops the next auxiliary term without a bound, the memory length is fitted, and the kernel's form is fixed by the quadrature, not by the eliminated dynamics. It is an augmentation with uncontrolled error, not the controlled one the question asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-761](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-761.md) | A continuous piecewise-linear function on R^d with compact support has a Fourier transform that, along any fixed direction û, is bounded by C(û)k^(−2), and by C(û)k^(−d−1) whenever û is orthogonal to no edge of its linear regions, which is almost every direction; C(û) is not uniform and grows without bound near the exceptional directions; for a ReLU network without compact support the statement is not established | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). One integration by parts turns f̃ into a sum of polytope transforms weighted by the region gradients and divided by k. Each further step of Diaz et al.'s recursion gains another 1/k until the path reaches a face whose directions are all orthogonal to k. Generic directions reach the vertices, giving k^(−d−1), and every direction gets at least k^(−2). It is a bound on what a piecewise-linear function contains, not a statement about training. Unbounded ReLU networks fall outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-762](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-762.md) | For a reversible diffusion dX = −∇U dt + √2 dW in equilibrium, an eigenfunction ψ of its generator with eigenvalue −λ is closed in conditional mean with no memory: E[ψ(X_{t+s}) \| the whole past] = e^{−λs}ψ(X_t), and so the same given ψ's own past; but ψ(X_t) is a Markov process in its own right only when \|∇ψ\|² is a function of ψ, since otherwise its own path reveals a noise intensity that its present value does not fix | The record's answer to what Nadler et al. ([LIT-1250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1250.md), read in [NOTE-986](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-986.md)) leave implicit when they call slow eigenfunctions reaction coordinates. Such a coordinate is exactly closed in its mean: its best prediction from the full state and from its own history coincide, with no memory term, and the Mori–Zwanzig memory and noise for it vanish under Mori's projection. It is closed in law only under a further condition. In the paper's examples the condition holds; the mixed Ornstein–Uhlenbeck eigenfunction x₁x₂ shows it can fail. This does not say that diffusion maps estimate the eigenfunctions well from finite data, or that a slow eigenfunction is the best coarse variable. | Active |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | For every α < 1/3 there is a nonzero weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, with velocity Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that vanishes outside a finite time interval; its energy is not conserved, so the energy flux across a mollification scale ε does not vanish as ε → 0, and it runs in both directions, out of the vanishing scales while the energy rises and into them while it falls | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-770](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-770.md) | In a closed population, any mapping of ancestors to descendants gives the Price equation: mean fitness times the change in mean character equals the covariance of fitness and character plus the fitness-weighted mean of the change in character, over any time interval and with no assumption beyond closure | Luque (2016), [LIT-205](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), §3, read in [NOTE-101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md), after Price (1970); the derivation re-derived by the promotion audit. An identity, not a model: it says nothing about which partition of the change a causal model licenses, predicts nothing until fitness and transmission are specified, and fails without closure (migration). | Active |
| [THEORY-771](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md) v3 | In a singularly perturbed system, fast states x̃ with dx̃/dt = f̃(x̃, y) + ε·δf and slow states y with dy/dt = ε·ḡ(y) + ε·δg, if f̃ is contracting in x̃ at rate β_f with x̃ = 0 an equilibrium for every y, ḡ is contracting at rate β_g, and \|δf\| ≤ d_f + α_f,x\|x̃\| + α_f,y\|y\|, \|δg\| ≤ d_g + α_g,x\|x̃\|, then for every ε below ε_c = β_f / [χ_f(α_f,x + χ_g α_f,y α_g,x / β_g)] the fast states stay within O(ε) of zero and, when d_g = 0, the slow states within O(ε) of the reduced trajectory, uniformly in time after a transient of order (1/β_f + 1/(εβ_g)) log(1/ε) | Bousquet and Slotine (arXiv 2015), [LIT-1292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1292.md), read in [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md). It gives Simon's near-decomposability the rate in ε that [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)'s open statement lacks: first order, for trajectory error, uniform in time, under contraction of the modules and of the reduced slow system, with an explicit, sufficient ceiling on ε. Deterministic. It bounds how far the states are from the reduced description, not how much information the rest of the system sends into the slow variables, and it takes the slow coordinates as given. | Active |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | For every β < 1/3 there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, in C⁰_t(B^β_{3,∞} ∩ L^{1/(1−3β)}), whose Duchon–Robert dissipation is the smooth nonnegative density E(t, x) = −e(t)e′(t)ρ₀(x₁, x₂)² fixed at the construction's first step; for such a solution the local coarse-grained energy flux into scales below ℓ converges, as ℓ → 0 and as a distribution in space and time, to E, so the transfer into vanishing scales is one-way at every place and time in the limit, nonzero inside a periodic array of pipes and zero outside them; where and how fast energy is dissipated is chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations, and nothing is shown about the sign at any positive scale | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) | In a singularly perturbed system ẋ = f(x, z, t), εż = g(x, z, ε), if g is contracting in z at rate λ_z for every x and ε, the reduced system ẋ = f(x, γ(x), t) on the slow manifold z = γ(x) is contracting at rate λ_x, f is α-Lipschitz in z, \|∂γ/∂x · f\| ≤ d and g is K-Lipschitz in ε, then for all t ≥ 0 the fast state is within χ_z e^{−λ_z t/ε}\|z(0) − γ(x(0))\| + εχ_z(d + K)/λ_z of the manifold and the slow state within χ_x\|x(0) − x_γ(0)\|e^{−λ_x t} + ε[C₁(e^{−λ_x t} − e^{−λ_z t/ε}) + C₂(1 − e^{−λ_x t})] of the reduced trajectory; partial contraction of f in x alone is not enough | Del Vecchio and Slotine (IEEE TAC 2013), [LIT-1295](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1295.md), read in [NOTE-1020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1020.md), with their Theorem 3's hypothesis corrected. A global, uniform-in-time, first-order bound on the error of the quasi-steady-state reduction, with every constant explicit and no requirement that ε be small. The reduction is Markovian: eliminating a fast, contracting variable costs O(ε) in trajectory error for all time, so no memory term is needed to that order. Constant metrics, deterministic, and the bound d on how fast the manifold moves is needed along the trajectory. | Active |
| [THEORY-775](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md) | With a Gaussian random-walk prior and an instantaneous unit-variance Gaussian encoder, the KL half of the evidence lower bound is the unordered slowness loss plus a constant; with a linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the bound is maximized on the span of the slowest SFA directions whose lag-one autocorrelation exceeds one half, with the basis inside that span unidentified, and on unwhitened input the maximizer is neither SFA's subspace nor invariant to rescaling the input | Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [LIT-1296](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1296.md), read in full in [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md). The ELBO of a dynamical VAE with prior N(z_{t−1}, I) and encoder N(g(x_t), I) is Σ E log p(x_t \| z_t) − ½Σ‖g(x_{t−1}) − g(x_t)‖² − (T − 1)d/2, an exact identity. For linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the maximizer spans the bottom eigenvectors of the difference covariance with eigenvalue μ < 1, each scaled by (μ^{−1/2} − 1)^{1/2} and then rotated arbitrarily. So it recovers SFA's slow span, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, not SFA's features. On raw input it trades variance against slowness. It says nothing about nonlinear encoders, about predictive sufficiency, or about Turner and Sahani's model. | Active |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | For every β < 1/3 and every smooth, strictly positive and strictly decreasing energy profile e(t) on [0, T], there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent β in space and time, with ∫\|v(t)\|² = e(t) at every time; for such a solution the energy flux across a mollification scale ε, integrated over any time interval, tends as ε → 0 to ½ times the drop in e, which is strictly negative, so energy leaves the resolved field for vanishing scales on every interval; this is one-way for the energy of the whole box, not at every point, and it is chosen by the prescribed profile, not forced by the equations | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls.
