Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | With a kernel normalised to unit diagonal, the kernel quantum relative entropy of two distributions is within O(σ²) of their Kullback–Leibler divergence as the bandwidth σ shrinks, for translation-invariant kernels on the torus generally and for kernels on other compact groups | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-812](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-812.md) | As dimension grows with the undersampling and sparsity ratios fixed, the ℓ₁ phase transition for recovering sparse vectors from random measurements sits at the same curve for a broad class of random-matrix ensembles, those with a kind of orthogonality or weak independence, as for Gaussian matrices, while differing at finite size | The general reading that [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to what 2,948,000 optimizations at three problem sizes showed. Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md), state it as the hypothesis of "weak universality" and pose the class of ensembles it holds for as an open problem. Nothing about non-Gaussian ensembles is proved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-819](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-819.md) | For an invertible map with an invariant measure, projecting onto the closed span of the whole past of chosen functions of the resolved variables (a Wiener projection) turns the exact discrete Mori–Zwanzig equation into one with no memory term: the next resolved value is a causal linear filter of those past functions plus a residual orthogonal to all of them, so the memory is carried by the coarse variable's own history; a finite NARMAX form follows only by a rational approximation of the filter, uncontrolled in general but exact for a scalar coarse variable of a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1) | Lin and Lu (2021), [LIT-1307](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1307.md), read in [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md). Mori–Zwanzig's memory is what a projection onto the present leaves out; a projection onto the whole past absorbs it, leaving the causal Wiener filter on the coarse variable's own history and a residual orthogonal to all of that history. Second-order (linear-span) projections, invertible dynamics and stationarity only. It gives no finite augmentation with a bounded error in general: the NARMAX step is the paper's uncontrolled approximation, exact only in the linear Gaussian class shown here. | Active |
| [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) v2 | For a stationary discrete-valued process X and any coarse-graining Z of its past, informational closure at every horizon is the same condition as zero one-step transfer entropy from the micro past, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, and as causal closure, Z's ε-machine coinciding with its υ-machine; for a coarse-graining of the present state it also makes Z's causal states a coarse-graining of X's, which does not imply closure, and the closed coarse-grainings are not closed under common refinement | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), with Barnett and Seth's definition ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md)). For discrete stationary processes, the information-theoretic criterion of emergent closure (dynamical independence), the interventionist one (the macro's own causal states are all the micro distinctions that matter for it) and, for maps of the present state, a computational one are nested as stated. The first two are one condition. It says nothing about approximate closure. It does not make closure a mark of unity. "Causal" is only in the Granger sense unless X is fully observed. | Active |
| [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | For every α < 1/15 there are weak solutions of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that satisfy the local energy inequality; in the construction their dissipation measure is a nonnegative function of time alone, equal at each time to the rate at which the total energy falls, zero while the local energy equality holds and positive on all of space during a short final interval in which the solution's energy is drained to zero; uncountably many such solutions share one initial datum and one dissipation measure; for them the local coarse-grained energy flux into vanishing scales converges to that measure, so the transfer is one-way at every place and time in the limit and spread uniformly over the box, with its timing chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. In the construction the dissipation measure is a function of time alone, so in the limit of vanishing scale the energy flux runs one way at every place, as in [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md), but in a Hölder class and spread uniformly over the torus rather than set in pipes. It is switched on only while the constructor drains the solution's energy to zero at the end of its life. Where, when and how fast the energy goes are inputs; the exponent is far from 1/3; nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-822](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md) | For a Markov chain and a partition of its states, strong lumpability, every state of a block sending the same probability into each block, is the column-equitability of the master-equation operator and makes the block label informationally closed; when the chain is irreducible, an informationally closed label that is itself Markov is strongly lumpable, with no aperiodicity needed; weak lumpability gives a Markov label that need not be closed; and the same holds on the causal-state chain of any stationary process | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), on Kemeny–Snell lumpability, joined to Shpak et al.'s column-equitable partitions ([LIT-1242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1242.md), [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md)). Exact closure of a block label in a Markov chain is a condition on transition rows, a symmetry, and not weak coupling. The converse needs the label to be Markov: a closed label can have memory. Exact results only, with no bound for nearly lumpable partitions. | Active |
| [THEORY-829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-829.md) | In Hrbacek's relative analysis, if belief at a context level is credence ultraclose to 1 at that level, the conjunction of any standard number of believed propositions is believed, while for an ultralarge number it can fail: in a fair lottery with an ultralarge number of tickets each 'this ticket loses' is believed and their conjunction has probability 0 | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), Ch. 3 (Stratified Belief, Def. 1; the Stratified Conjunction Principle, Def. 2, eq. 3.5 and §3.6.3.2), read in full in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md); re-derived by the promotion audit from finite subadditivity and Hrbacek's Closure principle. A result inside the framework: it says nothing about whether belief has levels, and any explicit level boundary collapses the model back to a fixed threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-847](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-847.md) | In a linear structural equation model whose exogenous micro-causes W₁, …, W_n drive effects Z = AW + F, with interventions that set all of W, all of Z or both, averaging each block is an exact transformation onto Ẑ = (an/m)Ŵ + F̂ if and only if every column of A sums to the same a, the column-equitability of the block of A from W to Z; the transformation is exact only for those whole-block interventions | Rubenstein et al. (2017), [LIT-1334](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1334.md), read in [NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), with Beckers and Halpern's restatement ([LIT-1316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1316.md), Example 3.3). Averages of linear micro-variables form a causally consistent macro model exactly when each micro-cause has the same total effect on the effect block. It says nothing about interventions on single micro-variables, which break exactness, nor about nonlinear or approximate aggregation. | Active |
| [THEORY-875](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-875.md) | Phenomenal binding of the parts of an experience can be modelled as agreement, on overlaps, of measured similarity structures assigned to the parts by a presheaf, and the broad quale is fixed by its parts exactly when that presheaf is a sheaf; a sheaf failure may mark disunity, as proposed for binocular rivalry, or context dependence within one unified experience, as in the Ebbinghaus illusion, and the framework does not yet say which | Lee-Youngzie, Tsuchiya, Robinson, Dietz & Monti (2026), [LIT-1352](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1352.md), read in full in [NOTE-1059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1059.md). A hypothesis article with no data. It proposes the presheaf and two readings of its failure, disunity for rivalry and context dependence for the Ebbinghaus illusion, without a criterion between them. It does not identify unity with a global section, since it assumes unity always holds. Its global section is measured data, its worked topology example is malformed, and by its own definition of gluing the rivalry case is not a sheaf failure. It answers [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) only by showing that a sheaf failure need not be disunity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-894](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-894.md) | A flow of pairwise comparisons on a graph splits orthogonally and uniquely into a gradient part, the l2-best global ranking, and a cyclic part, which splits into curl (local) and harmonic (global) inconsistency; a finite game's flow of unilateral payoff differences has no curl part, so every finite game is uniquely a potential game plus a harmonic game plus a nonstrategic remainder, and potential games are exactly those with no harmonic part; the decomposition is cardinal | Jiang, Lim, Yao & Ye (2011), [LIT-1439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1439.md), Theorems 4.7, 4.8 and 5.1: the Hodge/Helmholtz decomposition of edge flows, and HodgeRank's least-squares ranking with its curl and harmonic residuals. Candogan, Menache, Ozdaglar & Parrilo (2011), [LIT-1442](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1442.md), Theorems 4.1 and 5.1: every finite game is P ⊕ H ⊕ N, and potential games are P ⊕ N. Both read from arXiv; the proofs were followed. Settled as mathematics. Whether its shares measure a negotiation's potential depends on cardinal assumptions that the record's orderings do not supply. | Active |
| [THEORY-896](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md) | A finite game in strategic form has the finite improvement property, every path of strict unilateral improvements being finite, exactly when it has a generalized ordinal potential, a real function on strategy profiles that rises with every strict unilateral improvement; so in a finite game an ordering along which every improving move climbs exists exactly when there is no improvement cycle, and every sequence of improving moves ends at a pure equilibrium | Monderer and Shapley (1996), [LIT-1462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1462.md), unread: reported by Duersch, Oechssler and Schipper (arXiv 1003.4274) as Lemma 2.5. A finite game has the finite improvement property iff it has a generalized ordinal potential. The record proves the finite case here: a potential that rises with every improvement forbids cycles, and an acyclic improvement graph on finitely many profiles has an integer potential, the length of the longest improvement path into each profile. It is the precise form of "an ordering prevails" ⇔ "no improvement cycles", and it is ordinal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-916](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-916.md) | In the DeGroot–Friedkin model, where a group reaches DeGroot consensus on each issue and each member's self-weight on the next issue equals their control over the last, with fixed relative interpersonal weights, self-weights converge from every non-autocratic start to one equilibrium ordered by the eigenvector centralities of those weights: power accumulates above a centrality threshold, is autocratic exactly when the network is a star and democratic exactly when it is doubly stochastic, and members whom no path of influence reaches end with none | Jia, MirTabatabaei, Friedkin & Bullo (2015), [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md), read in [NOTE-1135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1135.md) from the version of record posted on the author's site; proofs skimmed. Theorems about a model, not findings about groups. The empirical companion, [LIT-1482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1482.md) ([THEORY-902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md)), uses anchored dynamics and a changing network, whose attractor is autocracy rather than this interior equilibrium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-924](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-924.md) | Elo ratings are the row means of a win-probability matrix's log-odds; they reproduce the matrix exactly when the log-odds have no cyclic component, and adding a copy of one agent shifts the ratings of the others | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Propositions 1 and 3 and appendix A, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. Elo is the uniform average of log-odds, and a fixed point matches only row sums. It is exact iff log-odds sum to zero around every triangle, so it has no predictive power in rock-paper-scissors, and duplicating an agent moves the ratings of agents that beat or lose to it. Cardinal throughout. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-926](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-926.md) | In a game where each player can transmit n bits before a win or a loss becomes unattainable, every antisymmetric pattern of wins and losses among ⌊2ⁿ⌋ strategies, a cycle through all of them included, is realized by some set of pure strategies | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Theorem 1 and Propositions 1–2, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proof followed. Strategies announce an identity, then throw or take the game as the pattern says. Go is at least about 1000-bit communicative (log₂ 180! ≈ 1094), so it has cycles of length 2¹⁰⁰⁰. Ordinal: only the sign of outcomes matters. The paper states it for patterns with draws too, which also needs a draw to stay attainable. The strategies are weak by construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-940](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-940.md) | In a finite symmetric zero-sum game, successive Nash clusters are weakly ordered by relative population performance, and a strategy that beats every member of a population containing a whole cluster lies in a strictly earlier cluster | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Definition 3 and Theorems 2–3, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proofs followed and re-derived. RPP is the population value of Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md). It holds for any Nash clustering of any finite symmetric zero-sum game and does not depend on the spinning-top hypothesis. The order is weak, since clusters can tie, and cardinal, since RPP uses payoff magnitudes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-944](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-944.md) | The value of the zero-sum game between two populations' evaluation matrices does not depend on which Nash equilibrium is used, is unchanged by adding agents that behave as mixtures of existing members, and is not positive for a population whose agents are all behavioural mixtures of the other's | Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md), Propositions 2 and 5, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1143.md), proofs followed and re-derived. Relative population performance is a game value, so equilibrium selection never arises. Behaviourally redundant members leave it unchanged, and a population contained in another's behavioural hull cannot beat it. It scores populations, not members, it is cardinal, and populations not nested by hull can still beat one another in a cycle. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-946](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-946.md) | In the zero-sum meta-game on an antisymmetric evaluation matrix the maximum-entropy Nash equilibrium is unique; when the meta-game has only one Nash equilibrium, adding exact copies of an agent splits that agent's mass evenly and leaves every Nash average unchanged; the equilibrium is uniform exactly when every agent's mean log-odds is zero, and uniform on the top-rated agents when the matrix is a pure gradient | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Proposition 4, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. The paper claims invariance to redundant copies without the uniqueness condition. Its proof covers the Nash set, not the maximum-entropy selection. A counterexample checked by script (one copy of a null agent moves an outside agent's Nash average from −0.5 to −0.2) shows the condition is needed. Cardinal: payoffs are log-odds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-971](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-971.md) | A unit that thresholds a pre-activation equal to a term depending only on one operand plus a term depending only on the other cannot be active on exactly the pairs with a given sum when that sum has two decompositions: if it is active on (x, y) and (z, w), it is active on (x, w) or on (z, y); so a sum computed from separately represented operands needs an earlier unit that combines them, as Ameisen et al. argue for addition in language models | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md), re-derived here. It is why their addition graphs contain "lookup table" features between operand features and sum features. Whether a given unit in a trained model meets the premise is an empirical matter: attention patterns that depend on both operands, or any earlier nonlinearity that mixes them, break it, and that mixing is exactly the intermediate step the result says is required. | Active |
| [THEORY-981](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md) | When a data distribution is unchanged by a group of orthogonal transformations under which a network is equivariant, the weights fixed by that group form a subspace that population gradient descent never leaves; for attention-only transformers on block-list inductive tasks, with fixed orthogonal write maps, Musat, Pimentel, Zucchet and Hofmann compute this subspace as the span of a few elementary token and position actions composed through the heads, and an elementwise optimizer such as sign descent keeps it only when those actions are aligned with the parameter coordinates | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). Symmetries of the data confine population gradient descent to the weights those symmetries fix; for their task class and idealized architecture this is a subspace whose coordinates are interpretable head actions. It does not say the subspace is attractive (the paper proves only invariance), and it does not cover minibatch noise beyond expectation, learnable value maps (a sketch in the paper), or adaptive optimizers, which keep it only when the basis is coordinate-aligned. | Active |
| [THEORY-1052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1052.md) | A quasi-static attractor describes an open system only while the drift of that attractor in state space is slow against the system's slowest relaxation, scaled by the distance to the tipping threshold; rate-induced tipping is the failure of that time-scale separation, and it can occur while the parameter itself moves slowly, if the attractor is sensitive to it, and with no slowing of any mode | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md). Shown for the linear tipping-radius model, where the sufficient condition for tracking is a rate comparison, and stated for a fast-slow example ("rate dependent tipping occurs when the slow and very slow timescales are no longer separable"). Proposed because for nonlinear systems the paper says "no exact analogy possible" and gives no general condition. It bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md), whose constraints hold over a window between time scales. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1054.md) | One arrangement of harmonic particles on a finite graph, with the same wiring, potential and inverse-mass response, gives the discrete wave equation when the integrator stores position and momentum and the discrete heat equation when it stores position alone; both are governed by the symmetrized graph Laplacian, and the coupling data do not decide between them | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. In the operad ArrSm, harmonic particles wired along a finite directed graph form one closed arrangement with potential Σ(κ_e/2)(q_tgt − q_src)². The phase semantics gives m_v q̈_v = −(L_G q)_v (Proposition 7.4.1) and a symplectic step; the configuration semantics gives m_v(q_v(t+1) − q_v(t)) = −(L_G q(t))_v (Remark 7.4.2). Active: both are short exact computations. It says nothing about time scales, and what differs between the two is a modelling choice, not the coupling. | Active |
| [THEORY-1056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1056.md) | In angular synchronization with outlier offsets, a polynomial-time spectral relaxation, the top eigenvector of the Hermitian matrix of measured phase offsets, recovers the angles once the share of good offsets exceeds about 1/√n on the complete graph, within a factor √((L − 1)/(2 log₂ L)) of the information bound that limits every algorithm, while exact maximum likelihood is a non-convex search costing O(mLⁿ) exhaustively; in this model the price of recovering the global configuration cheaply instead of optimally is a constant factor in evidence, which vanishes for L ≤ 6 | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §§2, 4 and 5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. The threshold p > 1/√n comes from a cited rank-one deformation theorem adopted to a non-Gaussian mixture and a heuristic comparison with random correlation, confirmed by simulation at n = 100 and 400; the near-optimality ratio compares it with an information bound for a different success criterion. Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1057.md) | Gradient descent with backpropagation, weight decay and Newton's method are one discrete-time semantics of an operad of potential-carrying lenses, in which the state moves by subtracting the sharpened sum of three pulled-back covectors (from the output, from the input wiring and from the potential); the semantics is an operad functor, so a composite's update is assembled from its parts' updates, and backpropagation is that functoriality | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. Lens internalization (Corollary 3.3.4) and an integrator give operad functors ArrSm → PC (Theorem 4.3.6, Corollary 6.4.1). Under the configuration integrator the state update is q ↦ q − ♯_q(ξ_Q), with ξ_Q the Q*-component of the sum in (58); a parameterized map wired to a loss gives gradient descent (76), a weight-only potential gives weight decay (Proposition 7.2.3), and an inverse-Hessian response gives Newton's method (67). Active as mathematics. Per datum, deterministic, explicit-Euler; Adam and momentum are conjectures. | Active |
| [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md) | The dynamics a coupled cell network admits, restricted to a robustly synchronous pattern, are dynamics admitted by a smaller quotient network whose cells are the synchronized classes, so behaviour of the quotient, including symmetric behaviour the original network has no symmetry to force, appears in the original as synchronous behaviour; the quotient admits more dynamics than restriction produces, and is unique only up to refinement of its arrow types | Stewart, Golubitsky and Pivato (2003), [LIT-1674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1674.md), read in [NOTE-1217](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1217.md): the quotient construction (§7), Theorems 8.3, 8.4 and 9.2 with proofs, the counterexample of Remark 7.5 and Example 7.1. Active as mathematics. The quotient describes the dynamics on the invariant subspace exactly, but only a subclass of the quotient's own admissible dynamics arises that way, and nothing is said about stability transverse to the subspace. | Active |
| [THEORY-1060](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1060.md) | Robinson's claim that sheaves are the canonical data structure for sensor integration rests on an axiomatization, not a theorem: six axioms are posited as what an integrated sensor system must be and a sheaf is defined as whatever satisfies them, the paper calls sheaves one of many co-universal information representations, and its consistency and fusion tools need only a presheaf | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3. A textual finding about the paper, Active as such. The word "canonical" is never defined for sheaves as a sensor model; its technical uses are the standard ones for cohomology. It does not say that sheaves are a poor model, or that no theorem of this kind could be proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-1062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1062.md) | On a discourse sheaf, where each agent expresses a private opinion through a linear map into each edge's space of topics, sheaf-Laplacian opinion diffusion converges to the orthogonal projection of the initial opinions onto the global sections, which are agreement in what each pair expresses and not in what they hold; stable polarized or incomparable private opinions are therefore possible, and when the sheaf has no nonzero global section the only limit is all opinions zero | Hansen and Ghrist (2020; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2021), [LIT-1646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1646.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1222](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1222.md) from the arXiv preprint. Active as mathematics: the convergence is a theorem about a linear heat equation, and the gap between expressed and held opinion is in the definitions and is worked in an example. It does not say that people reach agreement this way, or that an agreement in expression shows anything about what is held. | Active |
| [THEORY-1063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1063.md) | Black-boxing a passive linear circuit, which keeps only the Lagrangian relation its terminals' potentials and currents can jointly satisfy, is a hypergraph functor from open circuits to Lagrangian relations: the external behaviour of a circuit glued from parts is the relational composite of the parts' external behaviours, so circuits with the same behaviour are interchangeable in every composite, and the effective relation a composite presents at its boundary is fixed by its parts' black boxes alone | Baez and Fong (arXiv 2015, TAC 2018), [LIT-1644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1644.md), read in [NOTE-1223](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1223.md): Thm 1.1, proved as Thm 7.7, for circuits of passive, linear, two-terminal components over a field with positive elements, inductors and capacitors entering through the Laplace transform with zero initial conditions. The functor is not faithful, which is the point: circuits with one behaviour are identified. It says nothing about nonlinear or active components, and nothing in time-domain terms. | Active |
| [THEORY-1064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1064.md) | In counterexample-guided abstraction refinement, a spurious counterexample locates the distinction its abstraction lacked: walking it forward through the concrete system, the first abstract state where no concrete continuation exists merges the states the trace can reach with the states that have the transition onward, and splitting them removes the counterexample; for finite-state programs and ACTL* properties whose counterexamples are paths or loops, repeating check and split ends in a real counterexample or a proof | Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith (2000), [LIT-1652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1652.md), read in [NOTE-1231](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1231.md) from the authors' manuscript of the CAV paper. Active: the test for spuriousness (Lemma 1), the three-way cut at the failing state and the termination argument are given in full. The NP-hardness of the coarsest split is stated with its proof omitted, and the loop case rests on a theorem proved elsewhere. It does not say that the split found is the smallest, or how many rounds are needed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) | In a coupled cell network, a pattern of synchrony is invariant under every dynamics the network's architecture admits if and only if its partition of the cells is balanced, each cell of a class receiving, through each kind of arrow, the same number of inputs from each class; symmetry is one way to get balance and not the only one, so robust synchrony occurs in networks with no symmetry and among cells with no coupling between them, and the invariance says nothing about whether the pattern attracts | Stewart, Golubitsky and Pivato (2003), [LIT-1674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1674.md), read in [NOTE-1217](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1217.md) from the accepted version: Theorem 6.5 with proof, Lemma 6.3, worked examples without symmetry (Figures 3, 9, 15, 19). Active as mathematics. It generalizes [THEORY-276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md)'s orbit clusters. "Robust" means invariant for the whole admissible class, not stable, and not invariant for one model family; the paper studies "existence, not stability". | Active |
| [THEORY-1067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1067.md) | In angular synchronization from m pairwise offsets, each exact with probability p and otherwise uniform over L values, no estimator of any computational cost can recover all n angles with small error when p is below about √((n/m)·2 log₂ L/(L − 1)), nor an angle of average degree below about √((n/m)·log₂ L/(L − 1)), because each offset carries at most I(L, p) ≈ ½(L − 1)p² bits; below these thresholds a global configuration that exists is not determined by the pairwise evidence, whatever the resources spent on finding it | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. Active as mathematics: Fano's inequality applied to an explicit entropy count, asymptotic in m, n → ∞, p → 0 with L fixed. The bound is loose (it ignores the dependencies among offsets) and covers exact recovery and per-angle recovery, not partial correlation, which the eigenvector method achieves below it. It says nothing of what a bounded algorithm can do above it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1070.md) | For a weighted cellular sheaf of finite-dimensional vector spaces on a finite cell complex, the kernel of the degree-k Hodge Laplacian is the k-th sheaf cohomology, in degree 0 the space of global sections, and the linear flow ẋ = −Δ^k x converges exponentially to the orthogonal projection of its initial state onto that kernel, each eigencomponent decaying at its own eigenvalue; the inner products on the stalks are part of the data, so the same sections can come with different rates, and the Laplacian does not determine the sheaf | Hansen and Ghrist (2019), [LIT-1659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1659.md), read in [NOTE-1233](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1233.md) from arXiv v2: Theorem 3.1 (discrete Hodge theory), H^0 ≅ Γ (p. 7) and Proposition 8.1 (the flow), each with a proof; Fig. 3.1 for the Laplacian not determining the sheaf. Active as mathematics. The paper does not speak of relaxation rates or time-scale separation, does not say what produces the restriction maps, and treats only linear flows of a fixed Laplacian. | Active |
| [THEORY-1077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1077.md) | On a presheaf of pseudometric spaces, the consistency radius of an assignment, the largest distance between an observation and the restriction of another, is zero exactly for assignments induced by global sections (in metric spaces) and, when the restrictions are K-Lipschitz, bounds the assignment's sup-distance from every global section below by ε/(1 + K); so fusing data into a consistent state must move it at least that far, and the bound needs no sheaf condition | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Definition 20 and Propositions 21 and 23, read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3; both proofs checked. Active as mathematics. It does not say that the nearest global section is unique (the paper's Proposition 25 claims so for Banach sheaves and the proof does not reach it), that the radius locates a fault, or that a small radius means the data are right. | Active |
| [THEORY-1079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1079.md) | An open system can tip away from an attractor that exists, keeps its stability and keeps its basin at every frozen value of its parameter, when the attractor moves faster than the system can track it; with steady drift what bifurcates is the ability to track, in a co-moving frame, not the attractor, and the critical rate depends on the relaxation rate, the distance to the tipping threshold and the starting state | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md) from the corrected arXiv v5. Active as mathematics: shown in a linear model with a fixed stable matrix (so no bifurcation and no noise), in normal-form examples worked exactly, and in a fast-slow system whose equilibrium is unique and globally stable. It does not say that a system that tips is lost for good, that the threshold is a basin boundary, or that any real system has tipped this way. | Active |
| [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md) | On a connected graph whose edges carry phase shifts αᵢⱼ = −αⱼᵢ, the edge relations zⱼ = e^{iαᵢⱼ}zᵢ have a common nonzero solution, equivalently the twisted Laplacian Lα = δα*δα has a zero mode, exactly when the phase accumulated around every cycle is 0 mod 2π; otherwise each relation can be met alone but not all together, and the smallest eigenvalue of Lα, positive, measures the residual incompatibility, which on an isolated ℓ-cycle is largest at holonomy π | Torres-Hugas, Duch, Gómez and Arenas (2026), [LIT-1668](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1668.md), read in [NOTE-1218](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1218.md) from the arXiv preprint v2. The criterion is stated in the paper with an energy argument (pp. 2–3) and is the standard one for discrete magnetic and connection Laplacians, which it cites; the spanning-tree step the paper omits is written out below. The isolated-cycle spectrum is in closed form (eqs. 29–32). Both were checked numerically. Active: a theorem, with the qualification that it concerns the relaxed linear problem, not the phase dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-1088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md) | When the expression maps of a discourse sheaf diffuse to reduce disagreement, with opinions held fixed they converge to the nearest sheaf, in Frobenius distance, of which the opinions are a global section, so apparent consensus is reached by changing what is said ("learning to lie"); with opinions diffusing too the joint flow is gradient descent on ½‖δx‖², and conserved diagonal blocks of αδᵀδ − βxxᵀ keep the opinions from collapsing to zero; nothing in either flow checks an expression against the opinion it expresses | Hansen and Ghrist (2020; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2021), [LIT-1646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1646.md), §§8–9, read in [NOTE-1222](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1222.md) from the arXiv preprint. Active as mathematics: Theorems 8.1, 9.3 and 9.4 and Lemma 9.1. Theorem 9.3's proof is right only for α = β as printed; with the α, β weights it holds generally, which was checked numerically in the reading. The degeneracy guards are internal to the loop: minimal change and a conserved quantity, not evidence from outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1089](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1089.md) | In a passive linear network, eliminating interior nodes by the principle of minimum power, which over a general field with positive elements is stationarity, takes a Dirichlet form to a Dirichlet form on the remaining nodes, linearly in their values; eliminating one node s adds c_is·c_js/Σ_k c_ks to each coupling c_ij, so two resistors in series act at their ends as one of resistance r_AB + r_BC; composing Dirichlet forms by this elimination is associative but lacks identities, because an ideal wire of zero impedance has no power functional | Baez and Fong (arXiv 2015, TAC 2018), [LIT-1644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1644.md), read in [NOTE-1223](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1223.md): Thm 3.3, Lemma 3.4, Example 2.9 and Sec. 3.3. The elimination is what is usually called Kron reduction, a name the paper does not use. Over ℝ(s), with inductors and capacitors, the "minimum" is a formal stationarity condition, Kirchhoff's current law at interior nodes. The absence of identities is computed for a one-element set and asserted as typical otherwise. | Active |
| [THEORY-1090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md) | Eliminating an interior vertex of a cellular sheaf on a graph can leave its boundary a space of consistent assignments that no sheaf on the boundary vertices has: the interior can impose a constraint among boundary vertices that no set of pairwise compatibility conditions expresses, so Kron reduction, which turns the Laplacian of a connected graph into a graph Laplacian on any set of boundary vertices, fails for sheaves in general and holds when every vertex stalk has dimension at most one | Hansen and Ghrist (2019), [LIT-1659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1659.md), §4.2 (pp. 18–21), read in [NOTE-1233](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1233.md): a worked three-leaf star with a two-dimensional centre, and a closure theorem for the scalar-stalk case. Active as mathematics; the argument was checked. It is about the space of sections, a static fact; it does not say how often the obstruction arises, what structure would express the reduced constraint, or anything about dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-1092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1092.md) | Read over the sensor domains, the discrepancies between each observation and the restrictions of others can single out a faulty sensor where the consistency radius alone does not: in Robinson's simulated search, a 2° bearing bias was attributed to the right sensor, without prior knowledge of it, because every large discrepancy involved that sensor's domains, while the radius was lower than in the unbiased case | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Example 24, Case 2 (pp. 26–28 of arXiv v3), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md). One simulated case, one noise realization, read from a figure. Proposed until a stated procedure is tested over trials, including faults in the restriction maps, which enter the discrepancies in the same way as faults in the data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1094.md) | In counterexample-guided abstraction refinement the property and the concrete system are fixed inputs: the property's atomic formulas help build the first abstraction and no abstraction may merge states that disagree on them, every refinement only splits classes toward the concrete state space, and a real counterexample ends the procedure; so the loop revises which of the concrete system's distinctions the model draws, never the property or the space of possible answers | Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith (2000), [LIT-1652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1652.md), read in [NOTE-1231](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1231.md). A textual fact about the algorithm as specified in §§3–4, and the exact form of the limit the exchange of 2026-10-27 (A16 §6) gave for CEGAR as the formal neighbour of inquiry as specification ([CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md)). It does not say that a property cannot be revised by anyone, only that no step of this procedure does it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md) | Blackwell's comparison of experiments, its easy direction: an experiment is a family of distributions indexed by a common parameter, and if one experiment is a garbling of another by a Markov kernel, every risk attainable with the garbling in any decision problem with bounded losses is attainable with the original, on any outcome spaces | Split from [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)). [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)'s equivalence needs a second proof of the general converse and stays Proposed. Ten of its twelve dependents used only its definitions (an experiment, a garbling, the informativeness order), or only the easy direction, that a garbling never helps a decision-maker free to choose any rule. The easy direction holds on any outcome spaces, and its proof is two lines, re-derived below under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2's ruling, which [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps. It is Theorem 3 of Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md), and Blackwell's 1951 result. The finite converse is [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md), Active. | Active |
